title: Affine catenarity as a criterion on irreducible-closed chains
statement: Let $T$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and put $R=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. There is a homeomorphism $h:|T|\longrightarrow|\operatorname{Spec}R|$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For any prime ideals $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$ of $R$, the assignment $\mathfrak r\mapsto h^{-1}(V_R(\mathfrak r))$, where $V_R(\mathfrak r)=\{\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spec}R:\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak s\}$, is an inclusion-reversing bijection from the entire prime interval $[\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q]$ to the entire interval of irreducible closed subsets [def-weil-irreducible-components] between $h^{-1}(V_R(\mathfrak q))$ and $h^{-1}(V_R(\mathfrak p))$. It induces, by reversing the order of the images, a length-preserving bijection between finite strict chains with those endpoints, and this bijection restricts to the saturated chains. Here chain length is the number of strict inclusions, and a chain is saturated if no intermediate member of the corresponding interval can be inserted between adjacent terms. Consequently $R$ is catenary [def-exc-excellent-ring] if and only if, for every pair $Z\subseteq Z'$ of irreducible closed subsets of $|T|$, the lengths of finite strict chains from $Z$ to $Z'$ have a finite upper bound and all saturated chains from $Z$ to $Z'$ have the same length. Whenever these lengths are bounded there exists a saturated chain with the specified endpoints. The equivalence includes the empty affine scheme: its global section ring is the zero ring and both kinds of interval are absent.

source.place: Tag 02IH (lemma-catenary), using lemma-irreducible; affine presentation as in literature/stacks-project/schemes.tex Tag 01HW (definition-affine-scheme).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] with $X=T$ and $U=T$. Its isomorphism $T\cong\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ gives the required underlying homeomorphism $h$. This applies also to the empty affine scheme.

A homeomorphism gives mutually inverse inclusion-preserving maps on closed subsets by inverse image and image. These preserve nonemptiness and irreducibility: a decomposition into two closed proper subsets pulls back to such a decomposition, and applying the inverse homeomorphism proves the converse. By [def-weil-irreducible-components], $h^{-1}$ therefore bijects the irreducible closed subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with those of $T$.

source.place: Tag 02IH (lemma-catenary), proof using Tag 00ES (lemma-irreducible) and Tag 00NI (definition-catenary).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], $\mathfrak r\mapsto V_R(\mathfrak r)$ bijects primes with irreducible closed subsets and reverses and reflects inclusion. Compose with Step 2 to obtain $F$. Thus $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak q$ implies $F(\mathfrak q)\subseteq F(\mathfrak r)\subseteq F(\mathfrak p)$. Conversely, for any irreducible closed $W$ in this latter interval, take its unique preimage $\mathfrak r=F^{-1}(W)$; inclusion reflection gives both $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak r$ and $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak q$. This proves bijectivity on the entire interval.

source.place: Tag 02IH (lemma-catenary), proof using Tag 00ES (lemma-irreducible) and Tag 00NI (definition-catenary).

proof.text: For $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak r_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak r_n=\mathfrak q$, set $Z_i=F(\mathfrak r_{n-i})$ for $0\leq i\leq n$. Inclusion reversal and injectivity give a strict chain of length $n$. The inverse is $\mathfrak r_i=F^{-1}(Z_{n-i})$, so both composites are identities, also for $n=0$. Every possible insertion between adjacent $Z_i$ lies in the full endpoint interval; by Step 3 its unique preimage lies strictly between the corresponding adjacent primes. Conversely any prime insertion yields such a closed-subset insertion. Hence the bijection restricts to saturated chains.

source.place: Tag 02IH (lemma-catenary), proof using Tag 00ES (lemma-irreducible) and Tag 00NI (definition-catenary).

proof.text: In either type of interval with comparable endpoints, there is a finite strict chain: the two endpoints when distinct, or the singleton when equal. If all lengths are at most $N$, the attained lengths form a nonempty subset of $\{0,\ldots,N\}$ and hence have a greatest member $n$. Choose a chain attaining $n$. An insertion between adjacent terms would give length $n+1$, a contradiction. Thus there is a saturated chain; neither Noetherianity nor finiteness of the interval is needed.

source.place: Tag 02IH (lemma-catenary), proof using Tag 00ES (lemma-irreducible) and Tag 00NI (definition-catenary).

proof.text: Use the catenary clause of [def-exc-excellent-ring]: bounded finite strict chain lengths and equal saturated-chain lengths in each prime interval. Its Noetherian qualification concerns universal catenarity, not catenarity. Given $Z\subseteq Z'$, the global bijection $F$ gives unique primes $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$ with $Z=F(\mathfrak q)$ and $Z'=F(\mathfrak p)$. Step 4 identifies all chain lengths and all saturated-chain lengths in these intervals, so boundedness and equality hold on one side exactly when they hold on the other.

source.place: Tag 02IH (lemma-catenary), proof using Tag 00ES (lemma-irreducible) and Tag 00NI (definition-catenary).

proof.text: If $T$ is empty, the sheaf axiom for its empty covering gives a unique global section, so its section ring is the zero ring. This ring has no proper prime ideal, since its only ideal is the whole ring, and the empty space has no nonempty irreducible closed subset. There are no intervals to quantify over and both conditions are vacuous. Equal endpoints in any nonempty interval give the singleton chain of length zero.

lean.statement: theorem affine_catenary_chain_criterion (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine T] : ∃ (h : T ≃ₜ PrimeSpectrum Γ(T, ⊤)) (F : PrimeSpectrum Γ(T, ⊤) → IrreducibleCloseds T), (∀ r : PrimeSpectrum Γ(T, ⊤), (F r : Set T) = h ⁻¹' PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (r.asIdeal : Set Γ(T, ⊤))) ∧ (∀ (p q : PrimeSpectrum Γ(T, ⊤)), p ≤ q → ∃ e : Set.Icc p q ≃o (Set.Icc (F q) (F p))ᵒᵈ, ∀ r : Set.Icc p q, (e r).val = F r.val) ∧ (∀ (p q : PrimeSpectrum Γ(T, ⊤)), p ≤ q → ∃ e : {s : LTSeries (PrimeSpectrum Γ(T, ⊤)) // s.head = p ∧ s.last = q} ≃ {s : LTSeries (IrreducibleCloseds T) // s.head = F q ∧ s.last = F p}, ∀ s : {s : LTSeries (PrimeSpectrum Γ(T, ⊤)) // s.head = p ∧ s.last = q}, (e s).val.length = s.val.length ∧ (e s).val.toList = (s.val.toList.map F).reverse ∧ ((∀ i : Fin s.val.length, s.val i.castSucc ⋖ s.val i.succ) ↔ ∀ i : Fin (e s).val.length, (e s).val i.castSucc ⋖ (e s).val i.succ)) ∧ (IsCatenaryRing Γ(T, ⊤) ↔ ∀ Z Z' : IrreducibleCloseds T, Z ≤ Z' → (∃ N : ℕ, ∀ s : LTSeries (IrreducibleCloseds T), s.head = Z → s.last = Z' → s.length ≤ N) ∧ ∀ s t : LTSeries (IrreducibleCloseds T), s.head = Z → s.last = Z' → t.head = Z → t.last = Z' → (∀ i : Fin s.length, s i.castSucc ⋖ s i.succ) → (∀ i : Fin t.length, t i.castSucc ⋖ t i.succ) → s.length = t.length) ∧ (∀ Z Z' : IrreducibleCloseds T, Z ≤ Z' → (∃ N : ℕ, ∀ s : LTSeries (IrreducibleCloseds T), s.head = Z → s.last = Z' → s.length ≤ N) → ∃ s : LTSeries (IrreducibleCloseds T), s.head = Z ∧ s.last = Z' ∧ ∀ i : Fin s.length, s i.castSucc ⋖ s i.succ) ∧ (∀ p q : PrimeSpectrum Γ(T, ⊤), p ≤ q → (∃ N : ℕ, ∀ s : LTSeries (PrimeSpectrum Γ(T, ⊤)), s.head = p → s.last = q → s.length ≤ N) → ∃ s : LTSeries (PrimeSpectrum Γ(T, ⊤)), s.head = p ∧ s.last = q ∧ ∀ i : Fin s.length, s i.castSucc ⋖ s i.succ) ∧ (IsEmpty T → Subsingleton Γ(T, ⊤) ∧ IsEmpty (PrimeSpectrum Γ(T, ⊤)) ∧ IsEmpty (IrreducibleCloseds T))
